title: Heap buffer over-read in binaryMultiMMCPredictionEstimate for 4 <= L <= 16 (multi_mmc_test.h:38); reachable from a file, silent on a normal build
body:
## Summary

`binaryMultiMMCPredictionEstimate` (`cpp/non_iid/multi_mmc_test.h:33-40`) reads one byte past the end of the sample buffer for any input of **4 ≤ L ≤ 16 bits**. It is reachable from a file alone with the default command line, and on a normal (non-sanitizer) build it does **not** crash: the out-of-bounds byte is read from adjacent heap, folded into the MultiMMC prediction, and the tool prints an assessment and exits 0. AddressSanitizer flags it as a heap-buffer-overflow.

## Location

```c
// multi_mmc_test.h, binaryMultiMMCPredictionEstimate
assert(L>3);                                   // line 21: passes for L>=4
...
for(d=0; d<D_MMC; d++) {                        // D_MMC == 16 for the binary path
   curPattern = ((curPattern << 1) | (S[d]&1));
   (BINARYDICTLOC(d+1, curPattern))[S[d+1]&1] = 1;   // line 38: reads S[d+1], d up to 15 -> S[16]
   dictElems[d] = 1;
}
```

The init loop reads `S[d+1]` for `d` up to `D_MMC-1 = 15`, i.e. up to `S[16]`, with only `assert(L>3)` guarding entry. For `4 <= L <= 16` the index `d+1` runs past the buffer. (The generic/non-binary `multiMMCPredictionEstimate` guards the identical loop with `if(d < N)`, `N = L-2`, and is not affected; the binary path has no such guard.)

## Reproduction

Built at `87c104d` with AddressSanitizer (`-fsanitize=address,undefined -O1`, Apple clang; asserts left enabled, as in the shipped Makefile — no `-DNDEBUG`):

```
printf '\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x01' > f8.bin   # L = 8
./ea_non_iid f8.bin
```

ASan:
```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1
    #0 binaryMultiMMCPredictionEstimate(...) multi_mmc_test.h:38
    #1 multi_mmc_test(...) multi_mmc_test.h:154
    #2 main non_iid_main.cpp:453
0x... is located 0 bytes after 8-byte region
allocated by ... read_file_subset(...) utils.h:232
```

Every `L` in `{4,5,8,12,16}` reproduces; `L=3` aborts earlier on `assert(L>3)`, and `L>=17` is in bounds. On a stock build (no ASan) the same input prints a full assessment and exits 0 — the over-read is silent and its byte affects the reported figure.

## Impact

Reachable from an untrusted sample file with the default invocation (no `-l`, no special width). Out-of-bounds read of one byte that is incorporated into the estimate. Not a crash on a normal build, so it passes unnoticed; a hardened build (`_FORTIFY_SOURCE`, ASan, or a guard page) turns it into an abort.

## Suggested fix (not submitted as code here)

Guard the binary init loop the same way the generic path is guarded, e.g. iterate `for(d=0; d<D_MMC && d+1<L; d++)` (equivalently `d < N` with `N = L-2`), so `S[d+1]` is never read past the buffer.

Found during a memory-safety audit; reporting the memory-unsafe read on its own.
